deadline.value: No separate School of the Environment deadline is published; SGSR's Fall international F-1 applicant deadline is February 15, 2027 (general domestic regular deadline July 1; SGSR urges applying early so funding reviews begin in January).
deadline.quote: Fall (August to December) | April 1 | July 1 | February 15

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Environmental Science; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: The School of the Environment PhD pages do not state whether a faculty supervisor must agree before admission.

funding.value: The School of the Environment offers eligible students support through scholarships and work-study assistantships; SGSR states university assistantships and tuition awards are competitive and not guaranteed yearly.
funding.quote: The School offers eligible students support through scholarships and work-study assistantships.

also.quote: Tuition and assistantship awards are competitive and merit-based, and the School/College will award only a selected number of graduate students each Academic Semester. Funding is not guaranteed yearly

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter with a B.S. degree or a graduate degree in the natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, or a closely related area (3.0 / 'B' average in the last 60 B.S. credit hours).
entry_route.quote: Applicants for admission should have a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) or a graduate degree in the natural sciences, engineering, mathematics or a closely related area.

notes: Requires GRE General combined score of at least 300 (V+Q), 3 letters of recommendation, and Statement of Intent. Program page cites TOEFL >= 550 (paper-based; equivalent to FAMU's 80 iBT).
